analysis.title: ONEOK Inc. (OKE): 3Q26 Recap: Quieter Update, Though Generally Constructive Tone on Volume Growth
key_insights: OKE reported 3Q26 EBITDA of $2,238m vs GSe $2,191m and consensus $2,165m. Segment performance was broadly in line: stronger refined products margin from blending offset lower NGL results from lower Permian rates (higher ethane recovery).
FY26 EBITDA guidance was raised to $8.5-8.6b from $8.2-8.5b on stronger YTD results and initial Brazos contributions of $75m gross ($50m net of transaction costs).

Guidance implies 4Q26 EBITDA of about $2,194m, down 2% QoQ, or flat excluding $53m of transaction and debt benefits recognized in 3Q. GS sees potential 4Q outperformance because commodity and optimization assumptions look conservative.

Management gave a constructive 2027 outlook: full-year organic and inorganic contributions, broad volume growth led by Permian producer efficiency gains, and resilient Barnett Shale and Mid-Continent activity.
OKE has an upsized 1H27 hedge book at higher realized prices than 2026, which GS says could help offset year-over-year normalization of Waha basis spreads.

Management reaffirmed a mid- to high-single-digit EBITDA CAGR over five to seven years and expressed more confidence in reaching the upper end after Brazos integration. GS models about a 5% EBITDA CAGR and wants more confidence in underlying performance before going higher.

Legacy Brazos G&P throughput is tracking ahead of initial underwriting. 2026 Brazos EBITDA came in below expectations because of processing capacity in-service timing, with a larger step-up into 2027. The deal implied about $590m of 2027 EBITDA (about 7.5x including synergies).

OKE announced a 245 MBbl/d NGL pipeline expansion into the Northern Delaware by 3Q27, upsized on producer demand, with most volumes feeding its long-haul pipeline and fractionation system. Growth capex is quoted at $305m, and GS assumes about a 5x build multiple and a modest contribution until commitment duration and fee terms are known.
Medford Phase I and II enter service into 1Q27, so frac facilities should run at high utilization through 1Q27 to work through unfractionated NGL inventory built since 2Q26.

A second data center and power supply agreement of 110 MMcf/d supports a 500 MW plant entering service May 2028, following the earlier 250 MMcf/d agreement for a 1 GW plant in late 2030. GS views these as modest near-term EBITDA contributors.

Following the $9b Apollo structured equity investment, OKE lowered its leverage target to 3.25x net debt-to-EBITDA or lower from 3.5x. 2027 capex is near $3b versus about $3.5b in FY26, with $2.5-3.0b as the long-term normalized run-rate.

Capital returns stay focused on dividend growth with opportunistic buybacks. Management still wants accretive M&A, centered on NGL market share, but notes the pool of attractive deals has narrowed after sector consolidation.
GS raised EBITDA estimates through 2030 by about 1%, and is now about 1-3% above consensus. GS 2026E EBITDA is $8,678m vs consensus $8,524m and $8,613m prior.

GS keeps a Neutral rating and raised its 12-month price target to $93 from $91, using 10.5x 2027E EBITDA (from 10.25x) to reflect more clarity on long-term growth drivers. The stock closed at $95.82, 2.9% above the target.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $93 from $91 on a 10.5x 2027E EBITDA multiple (from 10.25x) after clearer long-term growth drivers. The stock at $95.82 sits 2.9% above the target.

sector_views.rationale: OKE is rated Neutral relative to its midstream coverage universe. GS is more positive on 2027+ volume growth but wants evidence of underlying performance and asset connectivity before raising its growth assumptions.

earnings_insights: OKE 3Q26 reported EBITDA $2,238m vs GSe $2,191m and consensus est $2,165m (reported 10/29/26 for the quarter).
3Q26 included $53m of transaction and minority equity sale adjustments.
FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to $8.5-8.6b from $8.2-8.5b. Implied 4Q26 EBITDA is about $2,194m, down 2% QoQ or flat excluding the $53m 3Q benefit.
Management pointed to about $100m of stronger base business performance vs 2Q26 expectations, most of which GS believes was already recognized in 3Q26.
GSe 2026E EBITDA $8,678m (prior $8,613m) vs FactSet consensus $8,524m. GSe 2027E $9,241m vs consensus $9,165m. GSe 2028E $9,860m vs consensus $9,706m.
GS 2026 capex estimate is about $3.4b vs guidance of about $3.5b and $3.2b prior. 2027 capex is near $3b, declining to about $2.5b+ in 2028+.
risk_factors: Upside risks: higher-than-expected synergy realization, higher commodity prices, higher project returns, stronger cash generation and capital returns, and Northern Border quality spec tightening.
Downside risks: expensive M&A, slower asset integration and synergy realization, higher competition for Permian NGLs, softer commodity prices, and project execution.
Implied 4Q26 EBITDA is lower, so the run-rate performance of the underlying business needs to be watched.
Waha basis spreads are normalizing year over year, which the larger 1H27 hedge book may only partly offset.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects higher 2027 growth than before the quarter, with Brazos throughput ahead of underwriting, a larger higher-priced 1H27 hedge book, Permian outperformance, and more confidence in the upper end of a mid- to high-single-digit EBITDA CAGR.
tension_points.bear_case: GS models only about a 5% EBITDA CAGR, wants more confidence in underlying performance and asset connectivity first, notes implied 4Q26 EBITDA is lower, and expects Waha basis spreads to normalize year over year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak base-business volume durability or an underwhelming project and contracting announcement for the Northern Delaware NGL expansion would undermine the growth view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Connectivity and processing plant additions through 2028 should deliver substantial NGL feedstock growth, with most Delaware volumes feeding OKE's own pipeline and fractionation system.
theme_stances.evidence: Management was most constructive on NGL supply growth
